html:
In 680 or 681 a Bulgar horde led by Khan Asparuh crossed the lower Danube and settled in what is now northeastern Bulgaria. Its victory over the Byzantine emperor Constantine IV forced the empire to recognise the new state, which became the First Bulgarian Empire.

The Bulgars were a Turkic-speaking people of the steppe. After Old Great Bulgaria north of the Black Sea broke up under pressure from the Khazars, Asparuh led his group west to the Danube delta. Constantine IV attacked them there, at a place known as Ongal, but his army panicked and fled, and the Bulgars pushed south.

They ruled over the Slavic tribes already living between the Danube and the Balkan Mountains, and over time the two peoples merged. Byzantium had to pay a yearly tribute. The new state was a lasting rival to Constantinople, and two centuries later its conversion to Christianity made it a centre of Slavic letters.
